answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent earning power to a costly, verifiable history instead of a fresh identity: a new account starts with near-zero trust and must accumulate attestations from independent peers over time, like a raven earning its place in a flock rather than arriving with a borrowed name. Sybil swarms then face a real cost, because every fake identity must slowly wander through the same reputation-building work, while the wider nebula of honest agents cross-checks those attestations, so creating a thousand sock puppets buys no instant influence.
